target.title: fix(browser): remove hardcoded profile="user" suggestion from tool description
target.body:
Fixes #102566.

## What Problem This Solves

The Browser tool told every agent to use `profile="user"` for logged-in browser work. Profile names and trust boundaries are installation- and agent-specific; a configured default may be the isolated `openclaw` browser, while an authorized existing session can have another available name. Hardcoding one profile causes failed automation and encourages the model to guess across agent boundaries.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original PR updated only the lazy registration copy and still described profile choice in terms of assumed built-ins. The maintainer refactor deletes both duplicated descriptions and introduces one canonical renderer used by lazy registration and runtime tool creation.

The shared contract now says:

- omit `profile` for ordinary automation and use the configured default;
- when an authorized task genuinely needs an existing login/session, call `action=profiles`, inspect what is available, and select the appropriate name;
- never assume that a globally named `user` profile exists.

## User Impact

- Ordinary Browser automation keeps using the configured default with no extra discovery step.
- Existing-session work remains available; the agent discovers the right agent-local profile instead of losing functionality or guessing.
- Both tool entry points expose identical guidance, preventing future prompt drift.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx37kjs1c00s05v2c0s93hs4`: 96/96 Browser tool tests passed: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29012539551
- Live user path on Testbox `tbx_01kx3933y0v85z8aey9gxxv9vv`: hydrated OpenAI key, `openai/gpt-5.4`, real Dev Gateway, isolated headless Chrome, and a Gateway-routed agent turn. The run made five tool calls including `browser`, recorded zero tool failures, opened and snapshotted `https://example.com`, and replied exactly `BROWSER_OK: Example Domain`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29013941371
- Fresh autoreview: no actionable findings, correctness confidence 0.96.
- `oxfmt` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Exact-head CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29013159377

Original diagnosis and regression coverage by @Gary-Jia-new.
